newsitem.title: USA: Business airfares to rise 8-9 pct in 1997 - study.
newsitem.headline: Business airfares to rise 8-9 pct in 1997 - study.

text.p: Business airfares will rise about eight to nine percent in 1997 due to slow airline capacity growth, strong passenger traffic levels and higher fuel costs, an American Express study said.

Airline industry load factors are expected to remain high, close to the record 70 percent reached this year. As a result, discount seats will be hard to come by for business travelers, the study found.
Overall, business travel prices will grow about six to seven percent next year as hotel, car rental and restaurant prices increase, the study said.

The seventh annual American Express study estimates that 1997 prices for corporate hotel accommodations will jump five to seven percent, while car rental prices will increase four to five percent and meal costs will rise by two to three percent.
Next year, spending on corporate group travel will grow by 10 percent, to almost $80 billion, the study said. For the past two years, corporate group travel has grown at a rate of 10 percent a year.
